concept_html:
Analysis code needs settings: a minimum base size, a weight column, a list of waves. Passing them around as a loose dict has three costs. A typo in a key ("min_bse") fails late or not at all. Nothing states which keys exist. Any function can change a value half way through a run.

A dataclass (Python 3.7 and later) turns the settings into a named, typed object.

from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReportConfig:
    weight_col: str
    min_base: int = 50
    waves: tuple[str, ...] = ()

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.min_base <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"min_base must be positive, got {self.min_base}")

What you get:

  • Named fields. cfg.min_bse raises AttributeError at once. Your editor and mypy see the fields.
  • frozen=True. Assigning a field raises dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError. Settings stay fixed for the run. Use dataclasses.replace(cfg, min_base=30) to build a changed copy.
  • __post_init__. Runs after the generated __init__. Put checks here so a bad config fails at load time, not in hour three.

Two traps:

  • Type hints are not checked at runtime. ReportConfig(weight_col="w", min_base="30") builds without error. Convert or check types in __post_init__, or use pydantic (lesson B5-L2) when input comes from files.
  • Mutable defaults. waves: list[str] = [] raises ValueError when the class is defined. Use field(default_factory=list), or an immutable tuple.

Load the config once at the edge, from YAML, JSON or arguments, and pass the object to the pure core.

lines: from dataclasses import dataclass
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReportConfig:
"""Settings for one reporting run."""
weight_col: str
min_base: int = 50
def __post_init__(self) -> None:
if not isinstance(self.min_base, int) or self.min_base <= 0:
raise ValueError(f"min_base must be a positive int, got {self.min_base!r}")
def suppress_small(counts: dict[str, int], config: ReportConfig) -> dict[str, int]:
"""Keep subgroups whose base reaches config.min_base."""
return {k: v for k, v in counts.items() if v >= config.min_base}

exercises.solution:
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReportConfig:
    """Settings for one reporting run."""

    weight_col: str
    min_base: int = 50

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not isinstance(self.min_base, int) or self.min_base <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"min_base must be a positive int, got {self.min_base!r}")


def load_config(raw: dict[str, object]) -> ReportConfig:
    """Build a ReportConfig from a parsed YAML or JSON mapping.

    Args:
        raw: Keys must match ReportConfig fields.

    Returns:
        A validated, frozen config.

    Raises:
        TypeError: On an unknown or missing key.
        ValueError: On an invalid min_base.
    """
    return ReportConfig(**raw)  # type: ignore[arg-type]

ValueError: On an invalid min_base.
"""
return ReportConfig(**raw) # type: ignore[arg-type]

title: Dataclasses as configuration objects
why_html:
A weighting script reads config["min_base"] from a dict built in a notebook cell. An analyst edits the cell to config["minbase"] = 30 for a test and forgets to revert. The script keeps using the old default of 50, so 14 subgroups the client asked to see are suppressed in the published tables. Nobody notices for two waves.

With a frozen dataclass, ReportConfig(minbase=30) raises TypeError: unexpected keyword argument at the first run.
